chapters.title: Preface to the 1992 Edition
chapters.sourcePressure: The preface frames the whole work as a pressure test for meaning, foregrounding Frankl staying in Vienna with his parents and placing witness before explanation.
chapters.coreMove: Test a claim about meaning against cost before you let it become comfort.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating the opening as a generic introduction to purpose or resilience.

chapters.title: Part One: Induction and Adjustments
chapters.sourcePressure: The early camp unit centers on arrival, shock, delusion of reprieve, selection, filth, beatings, suicidal thinking, and perception narrowing around survival.
chapters.coreMove: Recognize shock as a temporary survival narrowing before trusting the first story it produces.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning the camp arrival material into a general lesson about adapting to change.

chapters.title: Part One: Facts, Fulfillment, and Freedom
chapters.sourcePressure: Later camp life brings apathy, arbitrary fate, food fantasies, small decencies, beauty, faith, liberation, bitterness, and the narrow claim of inner freedom.
chapters.coreMove: Separate what fate controls from the small response that still belongs to you.
chapters.commonMisread: Claiming that attitude can overcome circumstances or that harmed people are to blame for suffering.

chapters.title: Part Two: Logotherapy in a Nutshell
chapters.sourcePressure: The theory unit explains logotherapy, the will to meaning, existential vacuum, noogenic neurosis, meaning through work, love, and attitude, plus paradoxical intention and dereflection.
chapters.coreMove: Translate emptiness into the next concrete responsibility rather than chasing mood relief.
chapters.commonMisread: Reducing logotherapy to finding your passion or using positivity to feel better.

chapters.title: Postscript: The Case for a Tragic Optimism
chapters.sourcePressure: The postscript defines tragic optimism through the tragic triad of pain, guilt, and death, insisting that optimism remains possible in spite of tragedy, not by denying it.
chapters.coreMove: Let pain, guilt, or death assign a bounded responsibility without pretending the tragedy is good.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning tragic optimism into cheerful reframing or a demand to be grateful for suffering.
